apikeys_create_description: A key grants the same access as DORMICE_API_TOKEN (the SDK, CLI, and E2B packages all accept it), but you can disable or revoke it here any time — no server config change, no restart.
apikeys_name_description: A human-readable handle, e.g. ci or laptop. Only one unrevoked key can hold a name at a time; once revoked, the name can be reused.
apikeys_expiry_description: Expires at the end of that day; you can extend or clear it later via Edit.
apikeys_created_description: This is the only time the key is shown — the daemon stores only a hash, and once this window closes it can never be retrieved. Copy it and store it safely now.
apikeys_copy_failed_manual: Copy failed — select and copy manually
apikeys_connect_copied: Setup copied — endpoint and token, two lines
apikeys_edit_description: Rename or adjust the expiry. The secret itself can never be viewed or replaced — to rotate it, revoke and mint a new key.
apikeys_revoke_description: Takes effect immediately and cannot be undone — clients still using it will get 401 on their next request. If you only need a pause, the enable switch is reversible. The record stays in the list as rotation history, and the name can be reused.
apikeys_revoked_toast: Revoked "{name}" — the next request will fail
apikeys_revoke_gone_toast: "{name}" is already gone — nothing was revoked
apikeys_bulk_revoke_description: {names} — takes effect immediately and cannot be undone; clients still using them will get 401 on their next request.
apikeys_env_row_title: Bootstrap/recovery credential from the server environment — rotating it means editing server config and restarting the daemon; the console cannot revoke it
apikeys_empty: No ledger keys yet — everything rides on the env credential above. Create one key per client, so a leak only means revoking that key instead of rotating everything.
apikeys_disabled_toast: Disabled "{name}" — you can re-enable it any time
